mainTopic: Which animals may redeem a פטר חמור: the משנה's list, בן בג בג's גזירה שוה from the קרבן פסח, and the questions of a בן פקועה, a נדמה and פסולי המוקדשין
overview: The משנה lists animals that may not be used to redeem a פטר חמור: a calf, a חיה, a slaughtered animal, a טריפה, a כלאים and a כוי. רבי אליעזר permits a כלאים but agrees about the כוי. The גמרא says the first view is בן בג בג's. He links the redemption lamb to the קרבן פסח through the word 'שה'. The doubled 'תפדה' still allows a female, blemished or older lamb, and each source limits the other. The גמרא then asks about a בן פקועה, and מר זוטרא and רב אשי argue whether it may be used. Next it asks about a נדמה according to the רבנן, but each attempted proof from a ברייתא is pushed aside. Finally it asks about פסולי המוקדשין, and רב מרי rules from the פסוק 'כצבי וכאיל' that they cannot be used. The amud ends with the גמרא starting to build a wider conclusion on that answer, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Animals that cannot redeem a firstborn donkey
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists six kinds of animals that may not be used to redeem a פטר חמור.
steps.simpleTranslation: You may not redeem a firstborn donkey with a calf, a wild animal, a slaughtered animal, a טריפה, a כלאים, or a כוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens with a list of animals that may not be used to redeem a פטר חמור. The Torah says to redeem it with a שה (a sheep or goat), and these animals do not qualify.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah requires a 'שה', and this list shows that not every animal counts. A calf is cattle, not a שה. A חיה is a wild animal. A slaughtered animal is no longer a live animal, and a טריפה is mortally damaged. A כלאים is a sheep-goat mix, and a כוי is a creature of doubtful status.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a fatal defect
A hybrid (here, a mix of sheep and goat)
An animal whose status is unclear: domestic or wild

steps.confusionAlert: The animal being redeemed is a firstborn donkey (פטר חמור). The animals listed here are the possible 'payment' animals, and the משנה is saying none of them work.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One may not redeem (a firstborn donkey)
neither with a calf nor with a wild animal,
nor with a slaughtered animal nor with a tereifa,
nor with a hybrid nor with a koy.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין פּוֹדִין לֹא בְּעֵגֶל וְלֹא בְּחַיָּה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A פטר חמור may not be redeemed with a calf, a חיה, a slaughtered animal, a טריפה, a כלאים or a כוי.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר permits the כלאים but not the כוי
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר disagrees about the כלאים, because it counts as a שה, but he agrees that a כוי may not be used.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר permits redeeming with a כלאים, because it is a שה. He forbids redeeming with a כוי, because its status is a doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר argues with one item on the list. He says a sheep-goat hybrid may be used to redeem, but he agrees that a כוי may not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אליעזר, a mix of sheep and goat is still a שה, since both parents are kinds of שה. A כוי is different: we do not know if it is a domestic animal at all, so it cannot count as a definite שה.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer permits redeeming with a hybrid
because it is a lamb,
but he forbids redeeming with a koy
because it is of uncertain status.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A dissenting view on one item of the previous list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, a כלאים may be used, but a כוי may not.

steps.title: A priest may not keep an unredeemed firstborn donkey
steps.stepSummary: If the owner gives the unredeemed donkey to a כהן, the כהן must first set aside a lamb in its place before he may keep it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he gave it to a כהן, the כהן may not keep it until he sets aside a lamb in its place.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a new rule about an owner who hands the unredeemed פטר חמור straight to the כהן. The כהן may not simply keep the donkey. He must first designate a lamb to take its place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The donkey has holiness that must be moved onto a lamb before anyone may use it. Handing it to the כהן does not remove that holiness. So even the כהן has to set aside a lamb in the donkey's place.

keyTerms.meaning: To keep it (for his own use)
That he set aside or designate

phrases.english: If he gave it to a priest,
the priest is not permitted to keep it
until he designates a lamb in its place.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן who receives an unredeemed פטר חמור must set aside a lamb in its place before keeping it.

steps.title: Whose opinion is the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds the first view of the משנה, which excludes all these animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the author of our משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by asking whose opinion the first part of the משנה follows. This sets up the next step, where the answer and its source are given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה excludes many animals without giving a reason. The גמרא wants to know the source behind this list, and which named authority holds it.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Whose opinion is our mishna?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds the list of excluded animals

steps.title: בן בג בג compares the lamb to the קרבן פסח lamb
steps.stepSummary: The משנה follows בן בג בג. He uses a גזירה שוה on the word 'שה' to apply the קרבן פסח's exclusions to the redemption lamb.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is בן בג בג, as a ברייתא teaches: The word 'שה' is said here, and 'שה' is said there (by the קרבן פסח). Just as there all these kinds are excluded, so here all these kinds are excluded.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה follows בן בג בג. It then quotes his teaching, which links the 'שה' of redemption to the 'שה' of the קרבן פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both verses use the same word, 'שה'. Through a גזירה שוה, whatever is disqualified for a קרבן פסח is also disqualified for redeeming a פטר חמור. A calf, a חיה, a slaughtered animal, a טריפה, a כלאים and a כוי cannot serve as a פסח, so they cannot serve here either.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
These 'names', meaning these categories of animals

steps.whyThisMatters: This גזירה שוה is the foundation of the whole sugya. The next steps test exactly how far the comparison to the קרבן פסח reaches.

phrases.english: It is the opinion of ben Bag Bag,
as it is taught in a baraita: Ben Bag Bag says:
It is stated here (redeeming the donkey) "lamb,"
and it is stated there (the Passover offering) "lamb."

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְּהַלָּן פְּרָט לְכׇל הַשֵּׁמוֹת הַלָּלוּ,
phrases.english: Just as there, all these types are excluded,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כָּאן פְּרָט לְכׇל הַשֵּׁמוֹת הַלָּלוּ.
phrases.english: so too here, all these types are excluded.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of authorship and gives the source
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows בן בג בג, who learns the exclusions from the קרבן פסח through a גזירה שוה on 'שה'.

steps.title: Must the lamb also be male, unblemished and under a year?
steps.stepSummary: If redemption is compared to the קרבן פסח, then the redemption lamb should also need the פסח's other requirements.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then just as there (פסח) it must be male, unblemished and in its first year, so too here it must be male, unblemished and in its first year?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges the comparison it just made. If we copy the קרבן פסח's rules, maybe we should copy all of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קרבן פסח must be male, without a blemish and less than a year old. If the גזירה שוה fully links the two cases, the redemption lamb would need these same qualities. That would be a much stricter law than we expect.

phrases.aramaic: אִי מָה לְהַלָּן זָכָר תָּמִים וּבֶן שָׁנָה,
phrases.english: If so, then just as there it must be male, unblemished and in its first year,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כָּאן זָכָר תָּמִים וּבֶן שָׁנָה?
phrases.english: so too here, must it be male, unblemished and in its first year?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מָה לְהַלָּן זָכָר תָּמִים וּבֶן שָׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes the גזירה שוה to its full extent
steps.kashyaTarget: The גזירה שוה comparing redemption to the קרבן פסח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the comparison works, it should bring in all of the פסח's requirements, including male, unblemished and under a year.

steps.title: The double 'you shall redeem' includes those lambs
steps.stepSummary: The Torah repeats 'תפדה' twice, and this ריבוי includes female, blemished and older lambs.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'תפדה' and again 'תפדה'. This repetition includes (more animals).
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the challenge with a second verse. Because 'you shall redeem' appears twice, the Torah is widening which lambs can be used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word is a ריבוי. It brings back in a female, a blemished lamb, and one older than a year. So the גזירה שוה still excludes the six animals in the משנה, but it does not bring in the פסח's requirements of male, unblemished and under a year.

keyTerms.meaning: It included (a ריבוי, which widens the law)

phrases.english: The verse states:
"You shall redeem," "you shall redeem": this includes (more).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by limiting the comparison
steps.terutzResolutionType: Second verse acts as a ריבוי that limits the גזירה שוה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The redemption lamb must match the קרבן פסח in every way.
steps.terutzMaskana: The doubled 'תפדה' allows female, blemished and older lambs.

steps.title: Then why not include all the excluded animals too?
steps.stepSummary: If the doubled 'תפדה' includes more, maybe it should include even the animals the משנה excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: If 'תפדה, תפדה' includes, then let it include even all of these (the animals in the משנה) as well?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. If the ריבוי is broad, why does it stop where it does?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ריבוי that widens the law might seem to undo all the exclusions. If so, the calf, the חיה and the others should also be allowed. That would contradict the משנה.

phrases.english: If "you shall redeem," "you shall redeem" includes,
then even all of these should also be included?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי תִּפְדֶּה תִּפְדֶּה רִיבָּה, אֲפִילּוּ כֹּל הָנֵי נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how far the ריבוי from the previous answer reaches
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Nothing in the ריבוי says it should stop short of the animals listed in the משנה.

steps.title: Otherwise the 'lamb' comparison would be useless
steps.stepSummary: If the ריבוי included everything, the גזירה שוה of 'שה' would have no purpose, so the ריבוי must be limited.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what would the 'שה, שה' comparison accomplish?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ריבוי cannot include everything. If it did, the גזירה שוה of 'שה' would teach nothing at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each source must keep some job. The גזירה שוה removes the six types of animals that are not a proper שה. The ריבוי only brings back qualities of an acceptable שה: female, blemished and older. In this way both sources stay meaningful.

keyTerms.meaning: What did it accomplish for him?

steps.whatToRemember: For בן בג בג, the גזירה שוה of 'שה' with the קרבן פסח excludes a calf, a חיה, a slaughtered animal, a טריפה, a כלאים and a כוי. The doubled 'תפדה' still allows a female, a blemished lamb or one older than a year. Each source limits the other, so both have a purpose.

phrases.english: If so,
what purpose does "lamb," "lamb" serve for him?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, שֶׂה שֶׂה מַאי אַהֲנִי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by showing the גזירה שוה must keep a purpose
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each source must have a purpose, so the ריבוי is limited
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ריבוי of 'תפדה' includes every animal, even those in the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The גזירה שוה still excludes the six types in the משנה. The ריבוי only includes female, blemished and older lambs.

steps.title: Can one redeem with a lamb taken from its slaughtered mother?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new question: may a פטר חמור be redeemed with a בן פקועה?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: what is the law about redeeming a firstborn donkey with a בן פקועה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question (איבעיא). It asks whether a בן פקועה, a live fetus removed from its mother after she was slaughtered, may be used to redeem a firstborn donkey.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know that a firstborn donkey is redeemed with a 'שה' and not with a slaughtered animal. A בן פקועה is strange because it is alive, yet halachically it may count as part of its slaughtered mother. So it is unclear which group it belongs to.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them (a real open question)
A live fetus found inside an animal that was slaughtered

phrases.english: A dilemma was raised before them:
What is the law about redeeming (a firstborn donkey) with a ben pekua?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic after the ריבוי discussion was settled in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a בן פקועה counts as a valid redemption animal (שה) for a פטר חמור.

steps.title: The question only applies according to the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא narrows the question. According to רבי מאיר a בן פקועה is a full שה, so the doubt exists only according to the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי מאיר there is no question. Since he holds that a בן פקועה needs its own שחיטה, it is a full-fledged lamb. The question only exists according to the רבנן, who say that slaughtering its mother makes it permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא clarifies whose opinion makes this a real question. It sets up the exact doubt that will be spelled out in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר requires a בן פקועה to be slaughtered on its own. That means he sees it as an independent living animal, so it is surely a 'שה'. The רבנן say the mother's שחיטה already permits it, so it is treated as if already slaughtered, and that is what creates the doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: Its mother's slaughter makes it permitted

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'מטהרתו' means the mother's שחיטה gives the fetus the status of a slaughtered animal. It is not נבלה, so it does not carry נבלה's טומאה, and it is permitted to eat.

phrases.aramaic: אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ,
phrases.english: According to Rabbi Meir, you should not ask this,
since Rabbi Meir says:
a ben pekua requires its own slaughter,
so it is a full-fledged lamb.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא כִּי תִּבְּעֵי לָךְ אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבָּנַן,
phrases.english: Rather, ask it according to the Rabbis,
who say: its mother's slaughter permits it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the question of step 10 to the רבנן's view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Limits the question to the opinion of the רבנן.

steps.title: Is it like meat in a pot, or a running lamb?
steps.stepSummary: The two sides of the question: is a בן פקועה treated like already-slaughtered meat, or does it count as a שה because it is alive and walking?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it like meat in a pot? Or perhaps, since right now it is at least running around, we call it a 'שה'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out both sides of the doubt according to the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: legally it is already 'slaughtered' through its mother, so it is like meat sitting in a pot, and one cannot redeem with a slaughtered animal. Side two: in reality it is alive and running, so it looks like and fits the name 'שה'. The question is whether its legal status or its living reality decides.

keyTerms.meaning: Meat in a pot (or basket), i.e., already-slaughtered meat
It runs and walks around (it is alive)
We call it by that name / the verse applies to it

phrases.english: Is it like meat in a pot,
or perhaps: since now, at any rate,
it runs and walks about,
we call it a "lamb"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the two possibilities behind the narrowed question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether legal 'slaughtered' status or physical aliveness determines if it is a 'שה'.

steps.title: מר זוטרא forbids and רב אשי permits
steps.stepSummary: Two אמוראים disagree: מר זוטרא says one may not redeem with a בן פקועה, and רב אשי says one may.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said: we do not redeem with it. רב אשי said: we do redeem with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a מחלוקת between אמוראים that answers the question in two different ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מר זוטרא sides with 'meat in a pot', so it cannot be used. רב אשי sides with 'it is running around', so it counts as a שה. The next step shows how they argue it out.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא, colleague of רב אשי
A leading late אמורא, editor of the תלמוד

phrases.english: Mar Zutra said: one may not redeem,
and Rav Ashi said: one may redeem.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the answers to the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A מחלוקת: מר זוטרא forbids redeeming with a בן פקועה; רב אשי permits it.

steps.title: רב אשי challenges מר זוטרא's comparison to פסח
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי suggests that מר זוטרא learns from קרבן פסח, and attacks this: if so, the redemption lamb would also need to be male, unblemished and within its first year.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to מר זוטרא: What is your reason? Because you learn from the קרבן פסח (where a בן פקועה is invalid)? If so, just as there it must be male, unblemished and in its first year, so too here it should have to be male, unblemished and in its first year!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי guesses the source of מר זוטרא's opinion and then challenges it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מר זוטרא likely relies on the גזירה שוה of 'שה' to פסח, where a בן פקועה is not valid. רב אשי pushes back: if you compare fully to פסח, then all of פסח's requirements should apply too. We know the redemption lamb has no such requirements.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as there... so too here (a comparison formula)
Male, unblemished, and within its first year

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same challenge as step 6. The גמרא is applying the earlier back-and-forth to this new case, not starting a new argument.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְמָר זוּטְרָא:
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Mar Zutra:
What is your reason? Because you derive it from the Paschal offering.

phrases.aramaic: אִי מָה לְהַלָּן זָכָר תָּמִים וּבֶן שָׁנָה,
phrases.english: If so, just as there it must be male, unblemished and in its first year,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כָּאן זָכָר תָּמִים וּבֶן שָׁנָה!
phrases.english: so too here it should be male, unblemished and in its first year!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְמָר זוּטְרָא: מַאי דַּעְתָּיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning behind מר זוטרא's ruling in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: מר זוטרא's comparison of the redemption lamb to קרבן פסח.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A full comparison to פסח would also bring in the requirements of male, unblemished and first-year, which do not apply to redemption.

steps.title: The double 'תפדה' removes the extra requirements
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא answers that the doubled word 'תפדה' widens the rule to include female, blemished and older lambs, while the comparison to פסח still excludes a בן פקועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'תפדה, תפדה' — the Torah included more (the other kinds of lambs).
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא answers רב אשי's challenge with the ריבוי from the doubled word 'תפדה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ריבוי includes lambs that are female, blemished or older, so the פסח requirements do not apply. The comparison to פסח still keeps its job of excluding things like a בן פקועה, just as step 9 showed that the ריבוי cannot cancel the גזירה שוה. So מר זוטרא's ruling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You shall redeem' written twice in the Torah

steps.whatToRemember: For מר זוטרא, the גזירה שוה to פסח excludes a בן פקועה, while 'תפדה תפדה' includes female, blemished and older lambs. רב אשי permits redeeming with a בן פקועה because it is alive and counts as a 'שה'.

phrases.english: "You shall redeem," "you shall redeem" — the verse included more.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's challenge from step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the comparison through a separate ריבוי in the verse
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Comparing to פסח would bring in all of פסח's requirements.
steps.terutzMaskana: The doubled 'תפדה' removes the requirements of male, unblemished and first-year. The פסח comparison still excludes a בן פקועה.

steps.title: If the doubled word widens the rule, include a בן פקועה too
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי challenges מר זוטרא: if 'תפדה תפדה' widens the rule, it should also include a בן פקועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the doubled 'you shall redeem' widened the rule, then even a בן פקועה should be included!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי attacks מר זוטרא's last answer. If the doubled word 'תפדה' adds female, blemished and older lambs, why shouldn't it also add a בן פקועה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: מר זוטרא used 'תפדה תפדה' to remove the קרבן פסח requirements (male, unblemished, first year). רב אשי argues that a widening phrase should widen all the way. Then nothing is left to exclude a בן פקועה, and redemption with one should be allowed, which is רב אשי's own view.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You shall redeem.' The word appears in two separate פסוקים (שמות יג:יג and שמות לד:כ), which suggests the rule is being widened.
It included or widened. A word in the פסוק adds more cases to the rule.

phrases.english: If 'you shall redeem,' 'you shall redeem' included more
phrases.notes: רב אשי quotes מר זוטרא's source back at him.

phrases.english: then even a בן פקועה should be included too!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי ״תִּפְדֶּה״ ״תִּפְדֶּה״ רִיבָּה, אֲפִילּוּ בֶּן פְּקוּעָה נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: מר זוטרא's use of 'תפדה תפדה' as a widening phrase
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A widening phrase should widen fully. If it removes the פסח requirements, it should also allow a בן פקועה.

steps.title: The comparison 'שה' to פסח must still exclude something
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא replies that if everything were included, the comparison 'שה' / 'שה' to פסח would have no purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what does the comparison 'lamb' / 'lamb' accomplish?
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא defends his position. The comparison to קרבן פסח through the shared word 'שה' must teach something, so it must still exclude the בן פקועה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה links פטר חמור to פסח through the word 'שה' in both places. If 'תפדה' widened the rule to include everything, that link would teach nothing. So the doubled word only removes the detail requirements (gender, blemish, age), and the link still excludes a בן פקועה, which is a more basic problem with whether it counts as a שה at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Lamb or kid. The shared word that links פטר חמור to קרבן פסח.
What did it accomplish for him? In other words, what purpose does it serve?

steps.whatToRemember: According to מר זוטרא, 'תפדה תפדה' removes the פסח details (male, unblemished, first year). The 'שה' comparison to פסח still excludes a בן פקועה.

phrases.english: If so, the comparison 'lamb' / 'lamb'
what purpose does it serve for him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's challenge in step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Every source must teach something: the 'שה' comparison would be pointless if everything were included.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The doubled 'תפדה' includes every kind of lamb, even a בן פקועה.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'תפדה' includes female, blemished and older lambs. The 'שה' comparison still excludes a בן פקועה.

steps.title: May one redeem with a נדמה?
steps.stepSummary: A new question: may a פטר חמור be redeemed with a נדמה, a lamb born of sheep that looks like a goat?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: what is the law about redeeming with a lamb that looks like a different species?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a brand-new question. It asks whether a lamb whose parents are sheep, but which looks like a goat, may be used to redeem a פטר חמור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether we go by the animal's parents or by how it looks. By its parents it is a real sheep, but by its appearance it looks like another species.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them. This is the standard opening for a new question.
An animal that looks like a different species than its parents.

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
What is the law about redeeming with a look-alike?
phrases.notes: For example, a lamb born of sheep that looks like a goat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question after the בן פקועה discussion ended.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a נדמה is a valid שה for redeeming a פטר חמור.

steps.title: No question according to רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא narrows the question: according to רבי אליעזר there is no doubt, since he allows even a hybrid.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי אליעזר, don't ask. Now that we redeem even with a hybrid, is it a question about a look-alike?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets limits on the question. It explains that according to רבי אליעזר the answer is obvious, so the question cannot be about his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר allows redeeming with כלאים, an animal that is half sheep and half goat. A נדמה actually comes from sheep, so it is surely no worse than a hybrid, and he would certainly allow it.

keyTerms.meaning: A hybrid. Here it means an animal born of a sheep and a goat.
Now. This word opens a 'now that... is it even a question?' argument.

phrases.aramaic: אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ,
phrases.english: According to רבי אליעזר, you should not ask
now that we redeem even with a hybrid,
is a look-alike even a question?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the question in step 18 by ruling out רבי אליעזר's view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which opinion the question actually applies to.

steps.title: The question is according to the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The question applies only according to the רבנן: do they reject only a hybrid, or also a נדמה?
steps.simpleTranslation: When should you ask it? According to the רבנן: maybe only a hybrid may not be used but a look-alike may, or perhaps there is no difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the real question. According to the רבנן, who do not allow a hybrid, is a נדמה allowed or not?
steps.deeperAnalysis: One side says the רבנן reject only a hybrid, which is truly a mix of species, while a נדמה is a real sheep by birth. The other side says that a lamb which looks like another species is treated the same as a hybrid.

keyTerms.meaning: When should you ask it? The phrase that sets where the question truly applies.

phrases.english: When should you ask? According to the רבנן:
is it only with a hybrid that we do not redeem,
but with a look-alike we do redeem,
or perhaps there is no difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves the question to the רבנן after ruling out רבי אליעזר in step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the רבנן treat a נדמה like a hybrid or allow it.

steps.title: A ברייתא about a cow that gave birth to a goat-like animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא: a goat-like animal born to a cow may not be used. It infers that a goat-like animal born to a ewe may be used.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: a cow that gave birth to a goat-like animal — one may not redeem with it. This implies that a ewe that gave birth to a goat-like animal — one may redeem with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to answer the question. It quotes a ruling and draws an inference from it, and the next step will work out whose opinion it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal born to a cow is not from the sheep or goat family at all, so it cannot be used. The ברייתא's choice of example implies that a goat-like animal born to a ewe, which is a נדמה, may be used.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear. The phrase that introduces a source brought as proof.
A goat-like kind. An animal that looks like a goat.
But this implies. The word that introduces an inference.

steps.confusionAlert: Only the first half, about the cow, is the actual ruling. The ewe half is the גמרא's own inference, introduced by 'הָא'.

phrases.english: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: פָּרָה שֶׁיָּלְדָה מִין עֵז — אֵין פּוֹדִין,
phrases.english: a cow that gave birth to a goat-like animal: one may not redeem with it,

phrases.aramaic: הָא רָחֵל שֶׁיָּלְדָה מִין עֵז — פּוֹדִין.
phrases.english: which implies: a ewe that gave birth to a goat-like animal: one may redeem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: פָּרָה שֶׁיָּלְדָה מִין עֵז
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to answer the question in step 20.
steps.raayaObject: That a נדמה may be used for redemption
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a cow that gave birth to a goat-like animal, and the inference about a ewe

steps.title: The ברייתא must follow the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא cannot follow רבי אליעזר, since for him the point would be obvious. So it must follow the רבנן, who therefore allow a נדמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? If you say רבי אליעזר, he redeems even with a hybrid! Rather, isn't it the רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא figures out whose view the ברייתא follows, to finish the proof. It concludes that it must be the רבנן, so they allow a נדמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר allows even a hybrid, so the ewe inference would teach nothing new according to him. It is meaningful only according to the רבנן, which shows they allow a נדמה even though they forbid a hybrid. The question form 'isn't it?' shows the proof is being offered and could still be challenged later.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, isn't it...? The phrase that pushes toward the remaining option.

steps.whyThisMatters: If this proof holds, the רבנן look at the parents, not the appearance. A נדמה born from sheep counts as a real שה even though a hybrid does not.

phrases.english: Whose view is this?
If you say it is רבי אליעזר,
but according to him we redeem even with a hybrid!
Rather, isn't it the רבנן?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun in step 21 by identifying whose view the ברייתא follows.
steps.raayaObject: The רבנן allow redemption with a נדמה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's ewe inference, which teaches something only according to the רבנן

steps.title: The ברייתא Can Still Follow רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back the proof. The ברייתא may follow רבי אליעזר after all, and it teaches that an animal follows its mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Really, the ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר. It teaches this very point: if a cow gives birth to a goat-like animal, you may not redeem with it. Do not say, 'Follow the animal itself, and this is a full goat.' Instead, follow its mother, and this is a calf.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from Step 22. It shows that the ברייתא is not pointless even for רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 22 said the ברייתא would be obvious for רבי אליעזר. Now the גמרא says it is not obvious, because we might have thought a goat-looking animal counts as a real goat. The ברייתא teaches that we follow the mother, so this animal is a calf, and a calf cannot redeem a פטר חמור. So the proof that the רבנן allow a נדמה falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / in truth (used to keep the original position)
It teaches us the point itself

steps.confusionAlert: Even if it looks exactly like a goat, an animal born to a cow is treated as a calf. Its status comes from its mother, not from its looks.

phrases.english: No, really it follows Rabbi Eliezer,
and it teaches us the point itself

phrases.aramaic: דְּפָרָה שֶׁיָּלְדָה מִין עֵז — אֵין פּוֹדִין.
phrases.english: that a cow that gave birth to a goat-like animal: one may not redeem with it.
Do not say: go after the animal itself,
phrases.notes: That is, judge by its own appearance.

phrases.english: and this is a full-fledged goat,
rather, go after its mother,
and this is a calf.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof made in Step 22
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the ברייתא must follow the רבנן
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא is not obvious for רבי אליעזר. It teaches that an animal follows its mother rather than its appearance.

steps.title: רבה בר שמואל's ברייתא on What Counts as a Hybrid
steps.stepSummary: A new attempted proof: a ברייתא calls a goat-like animal born to a ewe and fathered by a sheep a 'כלאים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear what רבה בר שמואל taught: What is a כלאים? A ewe that gave birth to a goat-like animal, and its father is a sheep.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא to try to settle the question about a נדמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case described is really a נדמה, since both parents are sheep but the baby looks like a goat. Yet the ברייתא calls it 'כלאים'. If a נדמה is treated like כלאים, it would be disqualified the way כלאים is.

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתָנֵי רַבָּה בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Come and hear, for Rabba bar Shmuel taught:
What is a hybrid?

phrases.aramaic: רָחֵל שֶׁיָּלְדָה מִין עֵז, וְאָבִיו שֶׂה.
phrases.english: A ewe that gave birth to a goat-like animal, and its father is a sheep.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתָנֵי רַבָּה בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected, a new source is brought
steps.raayaObject: Whether the רבנן disqualify a נדמה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבה בר שמואל

steps.title: That Is Not a Hybrid, It Is a Lookalike
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: if the father is a sheep, the baby is not a real כלאים. It is a נדמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If its father is a sheep, is it a כלאים? It is a נדמה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a problem in the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A real כלאים comes from two different species. Here both parents are sheep, so the baby is only a lookalike. The ברייתא's label 'כלאים' does not fit, so the גמרא must explain what it means.

keyTerms.meaning: Hybrid: offspring of two different species
An animal that looks like a different species from its parents

phrases.english: If its father is a sheep, is it a hybrid?
It is a lookalike!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the ברייתא just quoted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two sheep parents cannot produce a true כלאים. The case is really a נדמה.

steps.title: It Means: Treated Like a Hybrid by the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is reread. It means an animal similar to כלאים, which the רבנן treated as כלאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, read it this way: What is similar to כלאים, so that the רבנן made it like כלאים? A ewe that gave birth to a goat-like animal, and its father is a sheep.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the reading of the ברייתא. This sets up the claim that the רבנן treat a נדמה like כלאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is not saying the animal is truly כלאים. It is saying the Sages in general gave it the same status. If this ruling is about פטר חמור, it would answer our question: a נדמה is like כלאים, which the רבנן of the משנה do not allow.

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן made it equal / treated it as

phrases.english: Rather: what is similar to a hybrid,
that the Rabbis made it like a hybrid?

phrases.aramaic: רָחֵל שֶׁיָּלְדָה מִין עֵז, וְאָבִיו שֶׂה.
phrases.english: A ewe that gave birth to a goat-like animal, and its father is a sheep.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording problem of Step 25
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא calls a נדמה a true כלאים, which makes no sense
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא means the רבנן treated a נדמה like כלאים

steps.title: Which Law Is This About? Not Sacrifices
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which law this ruling is for. It cannot be קדשים, because a verse already disqualifies a נדמה there.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what law? If for קדשים, the same verse that excludes כלאים also excludes a נדמה. As a ברייתא teaches: 'שור או כשב' excludes כלאים, and 'או עז' excludes a נדמה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what law the ברייתא is talking about. It rules out קדשים first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For קרבנות, the Torah itself already excludes a נדמה from a verse. There would be no need for the רבנן to 'make it like כלאים.' So the ברייתא must be about some other law.

phrases.english: For what?
If for sacrifices:
from the place where it excludes a hybrid,
from there it excludes a lookalike,
as it is taught: 'an ox or a sheep' excludes a hybrid,
'or a goat' excludes a lookalike!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what law the reread ברייתא applies to
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which law the ruling 'the רבנן treated a נדמה like כלאים' is for

steps.title: Not About a Firstborn Either
steps.stepSummary: It also cannot be about בכור, since a verse already requires both mother and baby to be the same species.
steps.simpleTranslation: If for בכור, the Torah says 'אך בכור שור': only when it is an ox and its firstborn is an ox!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rules out a second option, the law of בכור. This sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For בכור, the Torah already requires the mother and the baby to be the same kind. So a נדמה is already excluded by the verse, and there is no need for a rabbinic comparison to כלאים. With both options gone, the ברייתא seems to point to another law, like redeeming a פטר חמור.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But the firstborn of an ox' (במדבר יח:יז)

steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן treat a נדמה like כלאים. That ruling cannot be about קדשים or בכור, since both already have verses that exclude a נדמה.

phrases.english: If for a firstborn,
the Merciful One said 'but the firstborn of an ox,'

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא הוּא שׁוֹר וּבְכוֹרוֹ שׁוֹר!
phrases.english: only when it is an ox and its firstborn is an ox!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי לִבְכוֹר, ״אַךְ בְּכוֹר שׁוֹר״ אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules out the second possible application, after ruling out קדשים
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The option that the ברייתא is about the law of בכור
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A verse already excludes a נדמה from בכור, so no rabbinic comparison to כלאים is needed

steps.title: The ruling cannot be about animal tithe either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries מעשר בהמה as the law the ברייתא is teaching. It rejects this, because a גזירה שוה on the word תחת already teaches that a נדמה is excluded from מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, maybe it is for מעשר? But that is learned from 'תחת' and 'תחת' from קדשים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests a third option, מעשר בהמה, for the ברייתא's ruling. It throws it out right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word תחת ('under') appears for קדשים ('under its mother') and for מעשר ('passes under the rod'). This links the two laws, so whatever disqualifies a נדמה for קדשים also disqualifies it for מעשר. That makes a separate ruling in the ברייתא unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: The animal tithe: every tenth animal is set aside as holy
'Under': the shared word that links קדשים and מעשר
He learns it, meaning it is derived from another source

phrases.english: Rather, maybe it is for the animal tithe?
But it is learned from 'under'–'under' from sacrificial animals!
phrases.notes: A גזירה שוה: ויקרא כב:כז ('under its mother') and ויקרא כז:לב ('passes under the rod')

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the process of elimination after קדשים and בכור were ruled out
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects מעשר as the law the ברייתא is teaching
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ruling would be redundant, since the גזירה שוה of תחת already covers it

steps.title: So the ruling must be about redeeming a firstborn donkey
steps.stepSummary: With קדשים, בכור and מעשר all ruled out, the only law left is פטר חמור. That would prove a נדמה cannot be used to redeem a firstborn donkey.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is for פטר חמור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its proof. The ברייתא must be teaching that a נדמה does not work for redeeming a פטר חמור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every other law already has its own verse covering a נדמה, so the ברייתא's ruling would be wasted there. The only place left for the ruling to do any work is פטר חמור. This answers the original question: a נדמה is not valid for redemption.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn male donkey, which must be redeemed with a lamb

phrases.english: Rather, it must be for the firstborn donkey.
phrases.notes: The only option left, which completes the proof

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the elimination of all the other options
steps.raayaObject: That a נדמה (or כלאים) may not be used to redeem a פטר חמור
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא calling a נדמה 'כלאים', which must be relevant to some law, and only פטר חמור is left

steps.title: The ruling may still be about tithe, for a baby with some of its mother's features
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The ברייתא can be about מעשר after all, in the case of a נדמה that has some of its mother's features. Without the ברייתא, one might have learned from בכור that such an animal is included.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, really it is for מעשר, in a case where the animal has some of the signs. You might have said: learn 'passing'–'passing' from בכור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. It shows the ruling can still be useful for מעשר in a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the baby has some of its mother's features, there is a second possible link: the word העברה ('passing') appears for both מעשר and בכור. Such a baby does count as a בכור, so one might think it also counts for מעשר. The ברייתא is needed to block that mistake, which means it is not wasted and no proof about פטר חמור follows.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Really' or 'actually': it returns to an option that was rejected
Some of the signs, meaning the baby partly resembles its mother
'You might have said': it introduces a mistaken assumption
'Passing': the shared word that links מעשר and בכור

steps.confusionAlert: There are two competing word-links here. תחת links מעשר to קדשים, which would exclude the animal. העברה links מעשר to בכור, which would include it. The ברייתא tells us which link wins.

phrases.english: No, actually it is for the animal tithe,
in a case where it has some of the signs (of its mother).
phrases.notes: A narrower case than a full נדמה

phrases.english: You might have said
that it is learned from 'passing'–'passing' from the firstborn,
phrases.notes: שמות יג:יב for בכור and ויקרא כז:לב for מעשר. Such an animal counts as a בכור (see טז:)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 30 by bringing back the מעשר option from step 29 in a narrower case
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof that a נדמה is invalid for פטר חמור
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The elimination was incomplete. מעשר still needs the ruling for an animal with some of its mother's features, because of a possible link from בכור
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Learn from בכור, through העברה, that an animal with some of its mother's features is included in מעשר

steps.title: The tithe law follows the link to sacrifices, so the proof falls
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא teaches that the link to קדשים through תחת wins over the link to בכור. An animal with some of its mother's features is therefore excluded from מעשר, and nothing can be proven about פטר חמור.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches us: learn 'under'–'under' from קדשים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its pushback. It states what the ברייתא is really teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's ruling has a real job: to decide that מעשר follows קדשים through תחת and does not follow בכור through העברה. Since the ruling is needed for מעשר, there is no reason to say it is about פטר חמור. The attempted proof fails.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It teaches us': it introduces the real point of the source
A link between two laws made through a shared word

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא is about מעשר. It excludes even a partial look-alike, because מעשר is learned from קדשים through תחת. The question of whether a נדמה can redeem a פטר חמור stays unresolved.

phrases.english: It teaches us
that it is learned from 'under'–'under' from sacrificial animals.
phrases.notes: The גמרא physically repeats the same words as step 29, now as the winning link

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the מהו דתימא / קא משמע לן structure of step 31
steps.terutzMaskana: מעשר is learned from קדשים through תחת, so an animal with some of its mother's features is excluded
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא's ruling is about מעשר, so it gives no proof about פטר חמור

steps.title: May a firstborn donkey be redeemed with a disqualified consecrated animal?
steps.stepSummary: A new question is raised: can a פטר חמור be redeemed using one of the פסולי המוקדשין, consecrated animals that became blemished and were redeemed?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: what is the law about redeeming with disqualified consecrated animals?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about which lambs are valid for redeeming a פטר חמור. It is setting up the next discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פסולי המוקדשין keep some holiness even after redemption: they may not be shorn or worked. The question is whether redeeming a פטר חמור needs the donkey's איסור to pass onto the lamb. If it does, that cannot happen on an animal that already carries an איסור. Steps 34 and 35 spell this out.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It was asked of them': a question raised in the study hall
Consecrated animals that became blemished and were redeemed, but are still forbidden to shear or work

phrases.english: A dilemma was raised before them:
What is the law about redeeming (a firstborn donkey) with disqualified consecrated animals?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: מַהוּ לִפְדּוֹת בִּפְסוּלֵי הַמּוּקְדָּשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about which lambs are valid for redeeming a פטר חמור, after the previous question was left unresolved
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a lamb from פסולי המוקדשין is valid for redeeming a פטר חמור

steps.title: The question only applies according to רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי שמעון, a פטר חמור is permitted for benefit and is just ordinary (חולין), so there is no question. The question only arises according to רבי יהודה, who says it is forbidden for benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי שמעון, you should not ask this question. Since he says a פטר חמור is permitted for benefit, it is ordinary (חולין). Where you should ask it is according to רבי יהודה, who says it is forbidden for benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is narrowing the question from the last step. It shows which opinion the question depends on, and this sets up the two sides of the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון and רבי יהודה argue whether a פטר חמור is forbidden for benefit. If it is permitted, as רבי שמעון holds, the donkey has no איסור to pass onto the lamb, so using a lamb from פסולי המוקדשין is no problem. Only according to רבי יהודה, where the donkey does carry an איסור, is there something to ask.

keyTerms.meaning: You should not ask this question (there is no question here)

phrases.aramaic: אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ,
phrases.english: According to Rabbi Shimon, you should not ask this question,
since he says it is permitted for benefit,
phrases.notes: He means the firstborn donkey (פטר חמור).

phrases.english: it is ordinary (non-holy),
phrases.notes: So there is no איסור to move onto the lamb.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: where you should ask it is according to Rabbi Yehuda,
who says it is forbidden for benefit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the question from Step 33 to רבי יהודה's view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which opinion about benefit from a פטר חמור makes the question about פסולי המוקדשין a real question?

steps.title: The two sides: does the prohibition move onto the lamb or just disappear
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי יהודה, maybe the donkey's איסור moves onto the lamb. In that case the lamb's existing holiness blocks it, because אין איסור חל על איסור. Or maybe redeeming only removes the donkey's איסור, since the lamb never becomes forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the law? Since the donkey is forbidden for benefit, do we say that one איסור cannot take hold on top of another איסור? Or perhaps, since the איסור does not move onto the redemption lamb, the redemption just removes the איסור from the donkey?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lays out the two possible ways to think about the question according to רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: redeeming moves the donkey's איסור onto the lamb. A lamb from פסולי המוקדשין already has its own holiness, and אין איסור חל על איסור, so the redemption cannot work. Side two: the lamb given to the כהן is permitted for benefit, so nothing moves onto it. Redeeming just cancels the donkey's איסור, and the lamb's earlier holiness causes no problem.

keyTerms.meaning: One איסור cannot take hold where another איסור already exists
Or perhaps (introduces the other side of a question)
Its איסור does not pass onto the item used to redeem it

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the lamb becomes forbidden according to רבי יהודה. Everyone agrees the כהן may benefit from the lamb. That fact is exactly why the second side says nothing moves onto it.

phrases.english: What is the law? Since it is forbidden for benefit,
do we say one prohibition cannot take hold on another prohibition?
phrases.notes: The lamb from פסולי המוקדשין already carries its own holiness.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא, כֵּיוָן דְּלָא תָּפֵיס פִּדְיוֹנוֹ,
phrases.english: Or perhaps, since its redemption item does not take on its status,
it is merely a cancelling of the prohibition?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי? כֵּיוָן דְּאָסוּר בַּהֲנָאָה, אֵין אִיסּוּר חָל עַל אִיסּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the two sides of the question now that it has been narrowed to רבי יהודה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does redeeming a פטר חמור move its איסור onto the lamb, which would block a lamb from פסולי המוקדשין? Or does it only cancel the donkey's איסור?

steps.title: רב מרי: consecrated animals are like a deer, so they cannot redeem
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי בריה דרב כהנא answers from the פסוק. The Torah calls פסולי המוקדשין "like the צבי and the איל". A deer cannot redeem a פטר חמור, so neither can פסולי המוקדשין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי, son of רב כהנא, said: Is what is written about them so small? The Torah says "like the deer and like the hart". Just as you cannot redeem a פטר חמור with a deer or a hart, so too you cannot redeem it with פסולי המוקדשין.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרי answers the question with a פסוק: you may not redeem a פטר חמור with an animal from פסולי המוקדשין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of deciding the logic question about איסורים, רב מרי points to a פסוק. The Torah compares פסולי המוקדשין to a צבי and an איל. A פטר חמור must be redeemed with a שה (lamb or kid), and a deer is not a שה. Because of this comparison, פסולי המוקדשין count as not fit for redemption either.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it so small? (it is significant)
Like the deer and like the hart (דברים יב:טו)
One may not redeem with them

steps.whatToRemember: A פטר חמור may not be redeemed with פסולי המוקדשין. The Torah compares them to a צבי and an איל, which are not a valid שה for redemption.
steps.whyThisMatters: The question is settled by a פסוק, not by the logic of אין איסור חל על איסור. So the two sides of the question from Step 35 stay undecided.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב מָרִי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Mari, son of Rav Kahana, said:
Is what is written about them insignificant?
"Like the deer and like the hart"?
Just as one may not redeem with a deer or a hart,
so too one may not redeem with disqualified consecrated animals!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מָרִי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא: מִי זוּטַר מַאי דִּכְתִיב בְּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from Steps 33 to 35 using a פסוק instead of the logic of איסורים.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. The Torah compares פסולי המוקדשין to a צבי and an איל, which cannot redeem a פטר חמור, so פסולי המוקדשין cannot either.

steps.title: Now that we have reached this answer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a transition: since רב מרי's reasoning from the פסוק has been accepted, it will now build a further conclusion on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you have arrived at this explanation,
steps.whatsHappening: This line does not teach a new law yet. The גמרא is setting up its next move by pointing back to רב מרי's answer and getting ready to draw a wider conclusion from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the question was asked only according to רבי יהודה. According to רבי שמעון the פטר חמור itself is permitted for benefit and counts as חולין, so there seemed to be nothing to ask. רב מרי's answer did not depend on איסור הנאה at all. It relied on the פסוק calling פסולי המוקדשין "like a צבי." Since that reason works no matter whose view we follow, the גמרא is preparing to apply it more broadly, beyond רבי יהודה alone.

keyTerms.meaning: That you have arrived at this (explanation or reasoning)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this line as a complete statement. It is only an opening phrase. The real point comes in the words that follow it.
steps.whyThisMatters: The phrase הַשְׁתָּא דְּאָתֵית לְהָכִי is a standard signal. When an answer turns out to rest on a stronger or different reason than the original question assumed, the גמרא uses this phrase to revise or widen its earlier assumptions.

phrases.english: Now that you have arrived at this [explanation],
phrases.notes: A transition formula. It refers back to רב מרי's proof from the פסוק that פסולי המוקדשין are like a צבי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds directly on Step 36. It takes רב מרי's answer from the פסוק as the new starting point for a broader conclusion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet. This is a setup phrase announcing that the reasoning of Step 36 will now be applied more broadly.
